title: Strategic value iteration with rounds of play and refit
question: Do rounds of play and refit (approximate policy iteration: play with the current policy plus 20% random actions, then value iteration on all data) give a better strategic policy than value iteration on random-action data alone (experiment 21)?
change: Experiment 21 plus 4 rounds: each round plays 100,000 games with the current policy and epsilon 0.2 (rl-value --driver eps:0.2:<policy>), then value iteration on all games so far (min-count 5).
method: Round 0 = experiment 21 (300k random-action games, policy-m5); rounds 1-4 of 100k games each; each round's policy on 2,000 validation seeds; the last on 10,000 evaluation seeds with rl-gate
setups: Perfection, 16×16 continents, 4 players, Crazy, seat 0 Xin-Xi (human seat), learner base greedy-full-probe-perf; opponents greedy-full-probe-perf, greedy-full-combo-perf, greedy-full-probe-perf (anchor), seats shuffled per seed (rl-gate defaults)
